title: I Used the Wood-Lathe Reservation on the Mentor Who Left a Tool in the Tailstock

parts.text: I unlocked lathe 3 at 2:33 p.m. and mentor Ash's gouge was still in my unpaid-looking leftover tailstock. The calendar said: BOOK THE LATHE. CLEAR THE TAILSTOCK. NO TOOLS LEFT. I was thirty-eight, member, holding a hold slip. Ash shrugged. "Mentors are the grain." I photographed the calendar, the slip, and the gouge. Then I logged an overlap. At 2:39 the shop manager pinged why Ash's name was on my tailstock. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop manager can see Ash's gouge in lathe 3's tailstock during my reservation.

social.video_title: The mentor left a gouge in my booked tailstock — Part 1/2
social.description: Wood lathe, a hold slip, a leftover tool. I logged the overlap. Would you have asked the manager?

parts.text: Ash called it a pause until the manager asked for the still. I printed the overlap, the calendar, and the slip. The gouge came out. Ash booked his own hour and told members pauses were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when tailstocks exist. Reservation now has a second line: MENTORS CLEAR THE TAILSTOCK. I keep lathe 3. Ash schedules. The shop finally looks like a hold, not leftover steel. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Overlap log, gouge out, and a second line. Was a pause ever my hold?
